content: 1. Healthcare professionals should actively screen for social determinants of health that may impact youth with type 2 diabetes. These include food insecurity, housing instability, limited health literacy, financial barriers, and lack of community support. These factors should be carefully integrated into the overall diabetes management plan to ensure comprehensive care. 2. It is essential for healthcare providers to utilize age-appropriate and validated screening tools to assess for diabetes-related distress, depressive symptoms, and disordered eating behaviors in youth with type 2 diabetes. When these issues are identified, timely referrals to behavioral health professionals should be made to address the psychological and emotional needs of the patient. 3. Preconception counseling should be provided to all individuals with diabetes who have childbearing potential. This counseling aims to optimize pregnancy outcomes by addressing diabetes management and related health considerations prior to conception. 4. Adolescents and young adults with diabetes should be screened for substance use, including tobacco, nicotine, alcohol, and other drugs, at the time of diagnosis. This screening should also be conducted periodically during follow-up visits to monitor and address any emerging substance use behaviors.
